newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chase ranked top in Asian derivatives - poll.
newsitem.headline: Chase ranked top in Asian derivatives - poll.

text.p: Chase Manhattan was named on Wednesday as the top house in Asian derivatives in a survey of derivatives dealers conducted by AsiaRISK, a quarterly supplement to RISK magazine.
Chemical Bank took the prize in 1995 but merged with Chase in March of this year.
Chase was ranked as one of the top three banks in 13 of 18 categories, which included interest rate swaps, currency swaps, currency options, forward rate agreements and foreign exchange forwards.
JP Morgan also put in a strong performance, winning more first places than Chase in some major categories but taking far fewer second and third places.
HSBC Markets dominated the Hong Kong dollar categories.
Citibank performed well in currency options, making a clean sweep of three categories -- Thai baht, Indonesian rupiah and Malaysian ringgit.

Prebon Yamane was voted the top derivatives broker, winning every category for which a top broker was named. In Hong Kong dollar-denominated interest rates and currency swaps, the top spot was shared with Tullet and Tokyo.
The results were calculated from a poll of more than 80 banks and other derivatives dealers in Asia, AsiaRISK said.
